# Text on each monitor

Tinta smooths its letters for the monitor the window is on: with that
monitor's gamma, its contrast and the order of its subpixels, as Windows'
ClearType tuner set them. To see it, open this page, drag the window to a
second monitor and back, and look at the edges of the letters below. On a
monitor whose subpixels run blue, green, red, or one turned on its side,
letters drawn for another monitor show coloured edges.

## Upright strokes

Thin upright strokes show a wrong subpixel order first, as a red edge on one
side and a blue one on the other:

Illinois lilt, minimum, HILLTOP, illicit, willfully, 1111 0101 |||| !!!!

*Illinois lilt, minimum, HILLTOP* and **Illinois lilt, minimum, HILLTOP**,
with a [link to the top](#text-on-each-monitor) and ==marked letters==.

### A smaller heading, with `inline code`

> A quote in softer ink: the fainter the letters, the more a wrong gamma
> shows, as strokes that look too thin or too heavy.

| Size   | Sample                    | Note                 |
|--------|---------------------------|----------------------|
| body   | The five boxing wizards   | jump quickly         |
| code   | `if (i == l) return 1;`   | upright and narrow   |
| strong | **Sphinx of black quartz** | *judge my vow*      |

1. Numbered, with H~2~O and x^2^ in small letters
2. A second line: lllll iiiii !!!!! |||||
   - nested, with `0O1lI` in code
   - [x] a ticked box
   - [ ] an open one

```cpp
// Code keeps its own face and the same smoothing
for (int i = 0; i < l; ++i) fill[i] = '|';
```

Chinese, Japanese and Korean letters are full of upright and level strokes:
中文排版 日本語の文章 한국어 문장, beside Latin letters and an emoji 🙂.
